max_bytes.description: The largest content one file version may have, in bytes; a bigger `create` or result answers `too_large`.

busy_retries.description: How often a lost compare-and-swap of the head is tried again from the fresh head before the write answers `busy`.

diff_lines.description: The most lines of the `diff` a write answers with; a longer one is cut and says `truncated`.

overwrite_hint.description: An `overwrite` that changes at most this share of the lines answers with `hint: use_replace`.

claim_ttl_s.description: How long, in seconds, the claim a path-taking write (`create`, the target of `move` or `copy`, `create_dir`) puts on its path stands when its writer never ended; the next writer of that path drops an older one. A living claim refuses a second writer with `path_taken`.

description.purpose: The one place content is made in a file space: `create`, every write op of `in_write` against the main line (compare-and-swap on the caller's `base`, a moved base merged three-way or refused as `base_moved`) or against a workspace's working version (`hop.ws`), and the content requests of `./ws` on `in_put` (`merge3`, `patch`, `create`). Content becomes content-addressed blocks under an immutable version; `./guard` checks it before it lands unless `force`. The structure ops of the main line live here too: `create_dir`, `remove_dir`, `move` and `copy` of a file, and `write_node` / `insert` at a node's anchor (`fh-...#<anchor>`, the head's span of lines, `base` the head). Every write that takes a path first claims it (a unique `claims` row), so two writers never land on one path.
description.use_when: Inside a file space only, behind `in_write` and `in_put`.
description.not_in_scope: No read op (`./read`), no workspace lifecycle or commit (`./ws`), no summary, embedding, node or directory count (`./derive`); no `move` or `copy` of a directory.
description.emits_meaning: `write_store` to `./store` between phases; `answer` once per `in_write` request, `put` once per `in_put` request; `in_check` to `./guard`; `in_derive` to `./derive` once per move of the main line (a `copy` included); `in_dirs` `{file}` to `./derive` once per main-line `remove` and `move`, because derive re-counts the directories above the file; `source_changed` with `tomb` once per main-line `remove`, after the tomb won (its node rows dropped in the tomb's bundle), and once per `move` with the head's node values and the new path (no derive job); `in_recover` to `./ws` when a due commit holds a file.
description.consumes_meaning: A request on `in_write` or `in_put` (a `create` or `overwrite` may take its content from `body.attachments[args.attachment]`, read by the code cell), the hook's answer on `checked`, and the store's answers to its own phases.
